components.note: 能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.pinyin: Tā de yǔyán nénglì hěn qiáng.
example.english: His language ability is very strong.
example.fact: 能 (from an old pictograph of a bear, prized for its strength) plus 力 (from a plow blade, standing for physical effort) combine into "capacity for strength" — a fittingly muscular etymology for the modern, abstract word for "ability."

examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu hěn qiáng de xuéxí nénglì.
examples.english: She has a strong ability to learn.
I'm not able to help you.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and prayer: 神, 礼, 福, 祈; 祝 is to wish.
兄 (older brother) — an opened mouth before the altar: the one who speaks the prayer or blessing.

example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ shēngrì kuàilè!
example.english: Happy birthday to you!
example.fact: 祝 is used in set greetings: 祝你好运 (good luck), 祝福 (blessings) and 祝贺 (congratulations). The pattern is 祝 + person + wish.

examples.english: Happy New Year to you!
Have a pleasant journey.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室; 完 first meant complete, whole.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; 元 also sounds out 玩 wán, 院 yuàn and 远 yuǎn.
羊 (sheep) — traditionally 羊 over 大: a big, fat sheep was good, tasty and pleasing, hence beautiful. 羊 also appears in 样 and 洋.

example.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén shì wánměi de.
example.english: Nobody is perfect.
example.fact: 完 ("complete, finished") and 美 ("beautiful") combine into "completely beautiful" — a vivid, almost poetic image for what English flattens into the single abstract word "perfect."

examples.hanzi: 这个计划看起来很完美。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà kàn qǐlai hěn wánměi.
examples.english: This plan looks perfect.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de tiānqì wánměi jí le.
examples.english: Today's weather is absolutely perfect.

components.note: 兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.

example.pinyin: Zhège zhòng wǔshí kè.
example.english: This weighs fifty grams.
example.fact: 克 is the gram in modern use (一克), and it means 'to overcome' in 克服 (overcome) and 攻克. In 巧克力 (chocolate) it is just a sound.

examples.pinyin: Zhè píng shuǐ yǒu wǔbǎi kè.
examples.english: This bottle of water weighs five hundred grams.
He worked hard to overcome the difficulties.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu wǔ kǒu rén.
example.english: There are five people in my family.
example.fact: 口 is the mouth and the measure word for family members (三口之家, a family of three), for mouthfuls and for things with openings like wells. It appears in 口语 (spoken language), 出口 (exit) and 人口 (population).

examples.english: Please open your mouth.
The train station has three exits.

components.note: 目 (eye) — an eye turned on its side. As a radical it marks sight: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睡 sleep, 盯 stare.
木 (wood) — 标 first meant the tip of a tree, hence a mark or target; wood radical as in 树 tree, 板 board.
票 (piào) is the sound in traditional 標; same series 漂 piāo and 飘 piāo; simplified 标 now shows 示.

example.hanzi: 我今年的目标是学会开车。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jīnnián de mùbiāo shì xuéhuì kāichē.
example.english: My goal this year is to learn to drive.
example.fact: 目 (eye) plus 标 (a marked tip or sign, originally the tip of a tree) combine into "what the eye is aimed at" — literally an archer’s point of aim, which is why 目标 covers both a literal physical target and an abstract life goal.

examples.english: What is your goal?
We finally reached our target.

components.note: 日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān shì jǐ yuè jǐ rì?
example.english: What is today's date?
example.fact: 日 is formal for 'day' in dates (五月三日) while in speech people say 号 (hào). It is also the short name for Japan (日本) and in 日子 (days, life).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shēngrì shì jǐ yuè jǐ rì?
examples.english: What month and day is your birthday?
Japan's cherry blossoms are famous.

meanings: to have sth to do with

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.

example.hanzi: 这本书跟中国历史有关。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū gēn Zhōngguó lìshǐ yǒuguān.
example.english: This book is related to Chinese history.
example.fact: 有关 can either follow a noun with 跟/与 ("X 跟 Y 有关", "X is related to Y") or sit in front of a noun as a compact attributive ("有关部门", "the relevant department") — two distinct grammatical slots for the same two characters that learners often only pick up one of.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì gēn wǒ yǒuguān.
examples.english: This matter has to do with me.

examples.hanzi: 有关这个问题,我们明天再说。
examples.pinyin: Yǒuguān zhège wèntí, wǒmen míngtiān zài shuō.
examples.english: As for this question, let's discuss it tomorrow.

components.note: 米 (rice) — refined grain gives the idea of essence and the best part, hence 精 fine, spirit (精神).
青 (qīng) is a near sound match (-ing); the series 青 清 请 情 晴 静 helps recall jīng.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.

example.pinyin: Lǎorén de jīngshén zhuàngtài hěn hǎo.
example.english: The elderly person's mental state is very good.
example.fact: Written identically, 精神 also has a second, differently-toned reading recorded in some dictionaries — jīngshen, with a neutral second syllable — meaning "energetic, full of pep" (他看起来很精神, "he looks lively"), distinct from the fully-toned jīngshén used here for the noun senses "spirit, mind, consciousness."

examples.english: I have no energy today.

examples.hanzi: 我们要学习他的认真精神。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào xuéxí tā de rènzhēn jīngshén.
examples.english: We should learn from his conscientious spirit.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the mouth/speech family, as in 吃, 叫, 问. Memory aid: set things apart by calling them out with the mouth — 另外 besides.
力 (strength) — the bottom. No reliable etymology. Memory aid: strength to pull one piece apart from the rest — 'another, separate'.
夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.

example.hanzi: 我买了一本书,另外还买了一支笔。
example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū, lìngwài hái mǎi le yì zhī bǐ.
example.english: I bought a book, and besides that I also bought a pen.
example.fact: 另外 works both as a stand-alone connective adverb ("besides, in addition," linking two clauses) and as an attributive right before a noun meaning "another, a separate" (另外一个问题, "another problem") — two overlapping but distinct jobs bundled into one word.

examples.pinyin: Lìngwài, wǒ hái xiǎng wèn yí jiàn shì.
examples.english: Also, I'd like to ask about one more thing.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge lìngwài de wèntí.
examples.english: This is a separate question.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.
木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 林, 桥; here a pine tree, the original meaning.
公 (gōng) is a loose sound clue for sōng; same series 颂 sòng, 翁 wēng.

example.hanzi: 周末我喜欢在家放松一下。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ xǐhuan zài jiā fàngsōng yíxià.
example.english: On weekends I like to relax at home for a bit.
example.fact: 放 ("to release, let go") and 松 ("loose, slack" — the same character that names the pine tree) combine into "release and loosen," a physical image of untensing muscles that maps neatly onto the modern sense "to relax."

examples.english: Listen to some music and relax.
Don't be nervous, relax!

components.note: 去 (to go) — 丢 looks like 去 with an extra stroke on top. Memory aid: something that 'goes' away is lost.
厶 (private, small) — the lower part, as in 去. The dictionary story (a lost piece of jade 玉) is a later reading, not proven.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de yàoshi diū le.
example.english: I've lost my keys.
example.fact: 丢 means to lose or throw away: 丢了 (lost), 丢人 / 丢脸 (to lose face). It is the casual word for losing things, whereas 失 appears in 失去.

examples.english: My wallet is lost.

examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ dōngxi diū zài lùshang.
examples.english: Don't leave things lying in the road.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住, 做.
木 (tree) — a person 亻 leaning on a tree 木: resting, hence 休息 rest and 退休 retire.
自 (nose) — over 心 heart: breath comes through the nose from the heart, so rest, news.

example.hanzi: 你工作太累了,应该休息一下。
example.pinyin: Nǐ gōngzuò tài lèi le, yīnggāi xiūxi yíxià.
example.english: You've been working too hard, you should rest a bit.
example.fact: 休 pictures a person 亻 leaning against a tree 木, and 息 combines 自 (nose) and 心 (heart) to depict the breath of life — 休息 pairs the image of "leaning to rest" with "catching one’s breath" into the everyday word for taking a break.

examples.english: I'd like to rest for a while.

examples.pinyin: Lèi le jiù qù xiūxi ba.
examples.english: If you're tired, go and rest.

components.note: 母 (mǔ) is a close sound clue for měi; the same part also in 海 hǎi, 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān dōu qù gōngyuán pǎobù.
example.english: I go jogging in the park every day.
example.fact: 每 ("every") almost always pairs with 都 later in the sentence to reinforce its all-inclusive meaning — dropping 都 after 每天 isn’t technically wrong, but native speakers rarely do, since the pairing is close to a fixed habit of speech.

examples.english: I take the subway to work every day.
She's happy every day.

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — written things and bamboo goods: 笔 pen, 第 order, 筷 chopsticks; 答 comes from bamboo slips used for replies.
合 (hé, together) — matching an answer to a question; sound is only loose, but 合 also sounds out 搭 dā.

example.pinyin: Qǐng huídá wǒ de wèntí.
example.english: Please answer my question.
example.fact: 回答 is reserved for answering a question or responding to something specifically asked — it isn’t interchangeable with 回复 (huífù), the word for replying to a message, letter, or email, even though both can be rendered as "reply" in English.

examples.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu huídá wǒ de wèntí.
examples.english: He didn't answer my question.

examples.hanzi: 这个问题你回答得很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí nǐ huídá de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: You answered this question very well.

components.note: 凶 (ominous) — an open pit 凵 with crossed marks inside: a trap, a sign of danger; seen in 凶手 murderer, 凶器 weapon.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá hái méiyǒu zhǎodào xiōngshǒu.
example.english: The police still haven't found the murderer.
example.fact: 凶 ("vicious, ominous" — pictured as something dangerous trapped in a pit) plus 手 ("hand," here meaning "the one who does it," as in 打手 "hired thug" or 选手 "competitor") combine into "the vicious hand" — the literal image behind the word for a murderer.

examples.english: The police are searching for the murderer.

examples.hanzi: 那部电影里的凶手是谁?
examples.pinyin: Nà bù diànyǐng lǐ de xiōngshǒu shì shéi?
examples.english: Who is the killer in that movie?

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and value: 财, 货, 买, 贵. 负 shows a person 人 carrying money: a burden, to bear or owe.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — 责 first meant demanding payment of a debt, hence duty. 责 sounds out 债 zhài, 积 jī and 绩 jì.

example.pinyin: Shéi fùzé zhège xiàngmù?
example.english: Who is in charge of this project?
example.fact: 负责 works as a plain verb taking an object (负责这个项目, "to be in charge of this project") but also shifts into an adjective describing a personality trait (他很负责, "he’s very conscientious") — the same two characters covering both a job description and a character trait.

examples.english: I'm in charge of this department.
He's very responsible about his work.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: an order is spoken.
令 (lìng, order) is a close sound clue for mìng; 令 also in 领 lǐng, 冷 lěng and 零 líng.

example.pinyin: Tā jiùle wǒ de mìng.
example.english: He saved my life.
example.fact: 命 means both 'life' (生命, 救命) and 'fate' (命运, 算命), and 'order' (命令). The word 命 in 救命 ('help!') is a common shout.

examples.english: The doctor saved his life.
He has good fortune.

components.note: 夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.

example.pinyin: Tā zài wàimiàn děng nǐ.
example.english: He is waiting for you outside.
example.fact: 外 is the opposite of 内 and 里: 外面 (outside), 外国 (foreign country), 外语 (foreign language) and 另外 (in addition). 外 can also be 'wife's side', in 外婆 and 外公.

examples.english: It's snowing outside.
He wants to study abroad.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 石 as in 破 break, 砖 brick: hard things colliding — 碰 is to bump into.
並 (bìng) — loose hint — 碰 is pèng; 並 (bìng) also sounds out 拼 pīn and 屏 píng.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zài lùshang pèngdàole lǎoshī.
example.english: I ran into my teacher on the road.
example.fact: 碰 means to bump or touch lightly and, with 到, to meet by chance: 碰到 / 碰见 (run into). It also appears in 碰运气 (to try one's luck) and 碰杯 (to clink glasses).

examples.english: Careful, don't bump your head.

examples.hanzi: 我在超市碰见了老朋友。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài chāoshì pèngjiànle lǎo péngyou.
examples.english: I ran into an old friend at the supermarket.

components.note: 人 (person) — the top. Common reading: a person standing between two sides, a go-between, as in 介绍 to introduce. Early forms may be armour.
八 (eight, divide) — Dictionary: a border dividing people. Memory aid: a person in the middle of two divided parts — in between.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.pinyin: Nǐ jièyì wǒ kāichuāng ma?
example.english: Do you mind if I open the window?
example.fact: 介意 shows up almost exclusively in questions and negative sentences (你介意吗? "do you mind?"; 我不介意 "I don’t mind") — using it in a flat positive statement ("我介意", "I do mind") is grammatical but sounds unusually blunt and confrontational in everyday speech.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú jièyì nǐ lái wǎn yìdiǎn.
examples.english: I don't mind if you come a bit late.

examples.hanzi: 他很介意别人怎么看他。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn jièyì biérén zěnme kàn tā.
examples.english: He cares a lot about how others see him.

components.note: 夕 (evening, night) — night and time: 外, 多, 夜; dreams come at night, so 夕 is the meaning clue; 林 is only filler.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zuówǎn zuòle yí gè mèng.
example.english: I had a dream last night.
example.fact: 梦 pairs with the verb 做: 做梦 (to dream). It also means a hope or ideal: 梦想 (dream, aspiration), 美梦 (sweet dream) and 噩梦 (nightmare). 梦 is also the first character of 红楼梦, Dream of the Red Chamber.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuówǎn zuòle yí ge hǎo mèng.
examples.english: I had a good dream last night.

examples.pinyin: Tā de mèngxiǎng shì dāng yīshēng.
examples.english: His dream is to be a doctor.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 读 read; testing often involves questions.
式 (shì) sounds exactly like 试 — a reliable sound clue.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 读 read; testing often involves questions.
式 (shì) sounds exactly like 试 — a reliable sound clue.

example.hanzi: 你要不要试试这个新餐厅?
example.pinyin: Nǐ yào bu yào shìshi zhège xīn cāntīng?
example.english: Do you want to try this new restaurant?
example.fact: 试试 is simply the verb 试 ("to try, to test") reduplicated — a common pattern also seen in 看看 ("take a look") and 想想 ("think it over") that softens a suggestion, making it sound more casual and tentative than the single-syllable 试 alone.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng shìshi zhè jiàn yīfu.
examples.english: I'd like to try on this garment.
It's okay, give it a try.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 部 part. 那 was a place name before it meant "that".
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒngyuǎn bú huì wàngjì nàtiān.
example.english: I will never forget that day.
example.fact: 那天 pins a memory or story to a specific, already-established day ("that day [we talked about]") — it needs shared context to refer back to, unlike 有一天 ("one day"), which introduces a brand-new, previously unmentioned day at the start of a narrative.

examples.hanzi: 那天我在家睡了一整天。
examples.pinyin: Nà tiān wǒ zài jiā shuìle yì zhěng tiān.
examples.english: That day I slept at home all day.

examples.hanzi: 你还记得那天说过的话吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ hái jìde nà tiān shuōguo de huà ma?
examples.english: Do you still remember what was said that day?

components.note: 糸 (silk thread; 纟 on the left) — ties and connections, as in 红, 给, 经. 系 is a link or relation.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and links, as in 红, 经, 系: thread gathered into one.
充 (chōng) is only a loose sound clue for tǒng.

example.hanzi: 这个系统出了一些问题。
example.pinyin: Zhège xìtǒng chū le yìxiē wèntí.
example.english: This system has some problems.
example.fact: 系 (originally silk threads linking together) and 统 (threads gathered into one continuous strand) both independently evoke things tied into a whole — 系统 layers two "connected-threads" images into the modern abstract word for an organized, interconnected system.

examples.english: The school's system is a little slow.

examples.hanzi: 人体是一个复杂的系统。
examples.pinyin: Réntǐ shì yí ge fùzá de xìtǒng.
examples.english: The human body is a complex system.

components.note: 目 (eye) — eyes and seeing: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睛 eyeball; sleep is when the eyes close.
垂 (chuí, droop) hints at the sound and the image: drooping eyelids. Also in 锤 chuí.
见 (see) — seeing and perceiving, as in 现, 看, 视: 觉 is to sense and become aware (jué), also "sleep" (jiào) in 睡觉.
The top is a shape of 学 (xué), a loose sound hint from the traditional 覺.

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān shíyī diǎn shuìjiào.
example.english: I go to sleep at eleven every day.
example.fact: 睡觉 looks like a fused single verb but is actually a verb-object compound that other elements can split apart — 睡了一觉 ("slept a sleep," i.e. "took a nap") and 睡午觉 ("take a midday nap") both insert material between 睡 and 觉, something a true single verb could never allow.

examples.english: I went to bed very early last night.
The child is already asleep.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 滚 is to roll like boiling water.
衮 (gǔn) — same sound — 滚 is gǔn, like 衮.

example.pinyin: Qiú gǔn dào zhuōzi xiàmiàn qù le.
example.english: The ball rolled under the table.
example.fact: 滚 is literally 'to roll' (滚动), and 'to boil' in 水滚了. As an imperative, 滚! means 'get lost!', which is very rude, so use it carefully; 滚蛋 is a similar curse.

examples.hanzi: 水已经滚了，可以煮面了。
examples.pinyin: Shuǐ yǐjīng gǔn le, kěyǐ zhǔ miàn le.
examples.english: The water is already boiling, so we can cook noodles.

examples.hanzi: 小球滚到沙发下面去了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo qiú gǔndào shāfā xiàmiàn qù le.
examples.english: The little ball rolled under the sofa.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — planning is done by talking things through; also 议 discuss, 论 discuss.
某 (mǒu) is a near sound match for móu; same part in 媒 méi and 煤 méi.
乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).

example.hanzi: 警方怀疑这是一起谋杀案。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng huáiyí zhè shì yì qǐ móushā àn.
example.english: The police suspect this is a murder case.
example.fact: 谋杀 specifically implies premeditation — the 谋 half literally means "to plot, to scheme" — distinguishing it from the broader 杀 ("to kill") or 杀人 ("to kill a person"), which make no claim about whether the killing was planned in advance.

examples.english: This murder case is very complicated.

examples.hanzi: 他爱看关于谋杀的小说。
examples.pinyin: Tā ài kàn guānyú móushā de xiǎoshuō.
examples.english: He loves reading novels about murder.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and worship: 神 god, 祝 wish, 福 fortune; 礼 are ritual courtesies.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ sòng gěi nǐ de lǐwù.
example.english: This is the gift I’m giving you.
example.fact: 礼 (rooted in 礻, an altar — its core sense is "ritual, ceremony") plus 物 ("object, thing") combine into "a ceremonial object" — a formal origin for the now-casual word for any gift, tracing back to the offerings exchanged during ancient rites.

examples.english: Thank you for your gift.

examples.hanzi: 生日我收到了很多礼物。
examples.pinyin: Shēngrì wǒ shōudàole hěn duō lǐwù.
examples.english: I received many gifts on my birthday.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 部 part. 那 was a place name before it meant "that".
禾 (grain) — crops, as in 秋 autumn, 租 rent, 和 and 秒 second; 种 is seed or to plant.
中 (zhōng) is a close sound clue for zhǒng/zhòng.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bù xǐhuan nà zhǒng diànyǐng.
example.english: I don't like that kind of movie.
example.fact: 那种 always needs a noun to follow it (那种电影, "that kind of movie") — for a stand-alone "that kind" without naming the noun, Chinese switches to 那样 ("like that") instead, since 种 is functioning here as a measure word, and measure words don’t usually stand alone without the noun they count.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi nà zhǒng shǒujī.
examples.english: I want to buy that kind of phone.

examples.pinyin: Nà zhǒng gǎnjué hěn nán shuō.
examples.english: That feeling is hard to describe.

components.note: 異 — the usual explanation is a figure holding something on the head, hence to put on or wear on the head.

example.pinyin: Tā dàizhe yì dǐng màozi.
example.english: He is wearing a hat.
example.fact: 戴 is the verb for putting on things worn on the head, face or hands: 戴帽子, 戴眼镜 (glasses), 戴手表 (a watch), 戴戒指 (a ring). Clothes use 穿, so 戴 and 穿 are a classic pair for learners.

examples.english: You should wear a hat when going out in winter.

examples.hanzi: 她今天戴了一条新项链。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān dàile yì tiáo xīn xiàngliàn.
examples.english: She wore a new necklace today.

components.note: 各 (each) — a foot 夂 arriving at a place 口: each one coming. 各 also sounds out 路 lù, 格 gé, 客 kè and 洛 luò.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.

example.hanzi: 各位好,欢迎来到我们公司。
example.pinyin: Gèwèi hǎo, huānyíng lái dào wǒmen gōngsī.
example.english: Hello everyone, welcome to our company.
example.fact: 各位 is a polite, slightly formal way to address a group — the natural choice for opening a speech, meeting, or announcement — while the more casual 大家 ("everybody") is the default among friends or in everyday conversation.

examples.english: Everyone, please sit down.
Everyone, please pay attention to safety.

components.note: 钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metals, as in 钱 money, 铁 iron, 铜 copper; 错 first meant to inlay metal.
昔 (xī) is a loose sound clue for cuò; 昔 also sounds out 借 jiè, 措 cuò and 惜 xī.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words and talk: 说, 话, 读; a spoken mistake or misunderstanding.
吴 (wú) gives the sound (wù, tone differs); same series 娱 yú and 虞 yú.

example.pinyin: Měi gèrén dōu huì fàn cuòwù.
example.english: Everyone makes mistakes.
example.fact: 错 (originally describing tarnished, mishandled metal) and 误 (originally a mistake made in speech) both independently mean "wrong, mistaken" — 错误 combines two near-synonymous "wrong" roots into one reinforced noun, the same doubling pattern seen in 喜欢 and 应该 elsewhere in this deck.

examples.english: This answer is wrong.

examples.hanzi: 他从错误中学到了很多。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng cuòwù zhōng xuédàole hěn duō.
examples.english: He learned a lot from his mistakes.

components.note: 子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de érzi.
example.english: He is my son.
example.fact: 子 is mostly a noun suffix pronounced neutral-tone zi: 桌子 (table), 椅子 (chair), 孩子 (child). On its own, zǐ means child or son and appears in titles like 孔子 (Confucius) and 君子 (gentleman).

examples.english: This child is very smart.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang yǒu yí ge bēizi.
examples.english: There is a cup on the table.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to follow is to move along behind someone.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do. 便 is a person adjusting things 更 to make them convenient (traditional explanation).

example.pinyin: Nǐ suíbiàn zuò, bú yòng kèqi.
example.english: Sit wherever you like, no need to be so polite.
example.fact: 随便 shifts easily between a relaxed, positive sense ("as you please, whatever works," 随便你 "however you like") and a mildly critical one ("careless, sloppy," 太随便了 "way too careless") — tone of voice and context, not the word itself, decide which reading applies.

examples.hanzi: 你想吃什么都可以,随便点。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng chī shénme dōu kěyǐ, suíbiàn diǎn.
examples.english: You can order whatever you like.
He speaks very casually.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.
发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).

example.pinyin: Tā de tóufa hěn cháng.
example.english: Her hair is very long.
example.fact: 头发 refers only to the hair on one’s head — body hair, animal fur, and plant fuzz all take the separate word 毛 instead, so "他有很多头发" strictly means "he has a lot of hair on his head," not hair in general.

examples.english: I got a haircut yesterday.

examples.pinyin: Tā de tóufa dōu bái le.
examples.english: His hair has all turned white.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 is grass and plants, as in 花, 草, 菜; hiding under vegetation — 藏 is to conceal or store.
臧 (zāng) — near sound — 藏 is cáng; 臧 also sounds out 脏 zāng.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ qián cáng zài chuáng xià.
example.english: He hid the money under the bed.
example.fact: 藏 has two readings: cáng ('to hide', as here) and zàng ('storehouse; Tibet', as in 西藏 and 宝藏). 藏 is the verb in the game 捉迷藏 (hide and seek).

examples.english: The kitten is hiding behind the sofa.

examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ lǐwù cáng qǐlái le.
examples.english: He hid the gift away.

components.note: 关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 父母一直很关心我的学习。
example.pinyin: Fùmǔ yìzhí hěn guānxīn wǒ de xuéxí.
example.english: My parents have always cared a lot about my studies.
example.fact: 关心 expresses caring through personal attention to someone’s wellbeing (关心某人, "to care about someone"), distinct from 关注 (guānzhù), which means to follow or pay attention to an issue, topic, or public figure without necessarily implying personal warmth.

examples.english: The teacher cares a lot about the students.
Thank you for your concern.

components.note: 广 (shelter) — buildings, as in 店 shop, 床 bed, 度 degree; 底 is the base of a house.
氐 (dī) is a close sound clue for dǐ; also in 低 dī and 抵 dǐ.

example.pinyin: Bēizi de dǐ shì hóngsè de.
example.english: The bottom of the cup is red.
example.fact: 底 is 'bottom' or 'base': 海底 (sea floor), 底下 (underneath), 到底 (in the end, 'on earth' for questions) and 年底 (year's end). 到底 is a typical emphatic question word, as in 你到底想要什么？

examples.pinyin: Hǎidǐ yǒu hěn duō piàoliang de yú.
examples.english: There are many pretty fish at the bottom of the sea.
Where on earth do you want to go?

meanings: variant of 幹嘛|干嘛[gan4 ma2]

components.note: 干 (dry; do) — a forked pole or shield. It lends its sound to 肝 gān, 杆 gān, 赶 gǎn, 汗 hàn and 岸 àn.
口 (mouth) — speech sounds and particles: 吧, 呢, 吃; 吗 is the question particle.
马 (mǎ) sounds like 吗 (ma) — same syllable, different tone.

example.pinyin: Nǐ gànmá bù zǎodiǎn gàosu wǒ?
example.english: Why didn't you tell me sooner?
example.fact: 干 is one of Chinese’s classic reading-switchers — pronounced gān it means "dry," but here, meaning "to do" (as in 干嘛/干吗, "to do what"), it’s read gàn; the two senses, merged into one simplified character today, trace back to separate traditional characters (乾 and 幹).

examples.english: Why are you looking at me like that?
What did he go off to do?

meanings: interest (thing in which one is interested)

components.note: 興 (traditional) — several hands lifting together, so to raise, stir, flourish. 兴 keeps only a few strokes; 高兴 is 'high spirits' and 兴趣 is 'interest'.
走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 起, 越, 赶: going toward something that attracts you.
取 (qǔ) is a close sound clue for qù; 取 also in 娶 qǔ and 聚 jù.

example.pinyin: Tā duì yīnyuè hěn gǎn xìngqù.
example.english: He's very interested in music.
example.fact: 兴趣 as a noun almost always appears inside the fixed frame "对...感兴趣" ("to feel interest toward...") — learners who try to use it as a plain verb the way English uses "to interest" often produce sentences that sound slightly off; the noun-plus-感 construction is the reliable default.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì Zhōngguó wénhuà yǒu xìngqù.
examples.english: I'm interested in Chinese culture.
What are your hobbies?

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.pinyin: Tā hěn zhòng gǎnqíng.
example.english: He is a very sentimental person.
example.fact: 情 is a bound form for emotions and circumstances: 爱情 (love), 友情 (friendship), 事情 (matter) and 情况 (situation). 事情 'matter, thing' is a common word that leans on this sense.

examples.hanzi: 你能说说当时的情况吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng shuōshuo dāngshí de qíngkuàng ma?
examples.english: Can you tell me what the situation was then?
They have a close bond.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 说 say, 问 ask; 告 is "to tell". 告 also gives sound to 造 zào and 靠 kào.

example.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān yào jiāo yí fèn bàogào.
example.english: I have to hand in a report tomorrow.
example.fact: 报 (a hand 扌 subduing a bound wrongdoer 卩 to announce a judgment) and 告 (mouth 口 plus ox 牛, "to speak with force") both independently carry a sense of "to announce, to inform" — 报告 doubles up two announcing-roots into the modern word for a formal report.

examples.hanzi: 经理向大家报告了计划。
examples.english: The manager reported the plan to everyone.

examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàogào xiě de hěn qīngchu.
examples.english: This report is written very clearly.

components.note: 人 (person) — one person following another: 从 means to follow, then "from".
氵 (water) — liquids and flowing; 没 first meant sink or submerge (淹没), which led to "gone" and then "not have".
殳 (shū) is only a loose sound hint for 没 (méi/mò); it also sits in 设 shè and 投 tóu.

example.pinyin: Wǒ cóngméi qùguò Xīzàng.
example.english: I've never been to Tibet.
example.fact: 从没 is short for 从来没(有) and is almost always followed by a verb marked with the experiential 过 (从没...过, "have never ever...") — dropping 过 in a 从没 sentence about past experience usually sounds incomplete to native ears, since 过 is what signals "at any point up to now."

examples.english: I've never seen snow.
He has never been late.

components.note: 夫 (man) is written twice, side by side — one man standing in for another, i.e. 'to replace, on behalf of' (替我 for me).
日 (sun) — the dictionary calls it a sound part, but tì ≠ rì, so treat that as unproven. Memory aid: two men take turns under the sun.

example.pinyin: Wǒ tì nǐ qù ba.
example.english: I'll go in your place.
example.fact: 替 works as a verb ('replace') and as a preposition 'for/on behalf of': 替我谢谢他 ('thank him for me'). It differs from 给 (gěi), which shows the receiver, whereas 替 shows the person you act in place of.

examples.hanzi: 你不舒服，我替你去开会。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù shūfu, wǒ tì nǐ qù kāihuì.
examples.english: You're unwell, I'll go to the meeting for you.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng tì wǒ xiàng nǐ māma wènhǎo.
examples.english: Please say hello to your mom for me.

components.note: 面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi de biǎomiàn hěn gānjìng.
example.english: The surface of the table is very clean.
example.fact: 面 means face, surface and side: 前面 (front), 外面 (outside), 见面 (to meet face to face) and 面子 (face, social prestige). 面 is also the character for noodles (面条) in mainland usage, a different word with the same shape.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi qiánmiàn yǒu yí ge rén.
examples.english: There's a person in front of the table.
Let's meet tomorrow.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.
力 (lì) sounds exactly like 历 — simplified 历 replaced complex 歷 with 力 for the sound; meaning is passing through time.

example.hanzi: 这是我人生中一次难忘的经历。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ rénshēng zhōng yí cì nánwàng de jīnglì.
example.english: This is an unforgettable experience in my life.
example.fact: 经历 names something a person personally lived through, usually over time (a hardship, a journey, a career) — its near-synonym 经验 (jīngyàn) instead names the practical know-how gained from doing something repeatedly, so a single dramatic event is an 经历, while years of practice building skill is 经验.

examples.hanzi: 这次经历让我学到了很多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì jīnglì ràng wǒ xuédàole hěn duō.
examples.english: This experience taught me a lot.
He has gone through many hardships.

components.note: 亠 (lid) — the top stroke group, as in 市 and 交. The sound-borrowed number; no meaning link. Memory aid: a lid on top of 八 (eight) ends up as six.
八 (eight) — the bottom part, as in 分 divide. Same shape as 'eight' but the number 六 does not come from it; use it as a visual memory aid.

example.pinyin: Xiànzài shì liù diǎn.
example.english: It is six o'clock now.
example.fact: 六 is considered lucky in Chinese culture because it sounds like 溜 ('smooth'), as in the saying 六六大顺 ('smooth sailing'). It also appears in 六一 (Children's Day, June 1).

examples.english: I get up at six.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bān yǒu liù ge nǚshēng.
examples.english: There are six girls in this class.

components.note: 飞 (fly) — simplified from 飛, a bird with spread wings.

example.pinyin: Niǎo zài tiān shang fēi.
example.english: Birds fly in the sky.
example.fact: 飞 is to fly and to go quickly: 飞机 (airplane), 飞行 (flight), 起飞 (take off), and 飞快 (very fast). People also say 飞 casually for 'go by plane': 我明天飞北京.

examples.pinyin: Fēijī míngtiān zǎoshang bā diǎn fēi.
examples.english: The plane flies at eight tomorrow morning.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zuò fēijī qù Běijīng.
examples.english: I want to take a plane to Beijing.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen de lǎoshī fēicháng rènzhēn.
example.english: Our teacher is extremely conscientious.
example.fact: 老师 has increasingly become a generic polite address term even outside the classroom — waitstaff, strangers giving directions, or hosts on a talk show may all be addressed as 老师 as a mark of respect for perceived expertise, not because they are literally anyone’s teacher.

examples.english: The teacher is writing on the blackboard.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng dāng yì míng lǎoshī.
examples.english: He wants to be a teacher.
